title: اتجاهات طلبة الإعلام نحو مصادر أخبار الإعلام التقليدي والرقمي (كليتيّ الإعلام في جامعتيّ البترا واليرموك أنموذجاً)
journal: Arabian Gulf Journal of Humanities and Social Studies

title: Досвід країн ЄС у державному регулюванні людського розвитку: імплікації для повоєнного відновлення України The EU Countries’ Experience in State Regulation of Human Development: Implications for the Post-War Recovery of Ukraine
journal: Bulletin of the Academy of Labor, Social Relations and Tourism. Series: Economics, Psychology and Management
abstract: Ukraine’s post-war recovery critically depends on human capital, yet the European Union’s experience in the state regulation of human development remains fragmented and unsystematized regarding its applicability to a reconstructing country. The article aims to systematize the instruments and mechanisms of state regulation of human development across EU countries and to assess their applicability to Ukraine’s post-war recovery. A conceptual-analytical policy review was adopted – a structured narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature. The study hypothesizes that the toolkit’s applicability is not a property of individual instruments but a conditional, sequenced configuration in which institutional absorptive capacity is the binding precondition. A corpus of 33 sources was grouped into four thematic clusters; a uniform set of parameters was extracted from each; six axes of tension were derived; and the instruments were classified by mechanism of action and level of application. Six instrument types and three cross-cutting interaction mechanisms were systematized. It was established that institutional absorptive capacity is the meta-condition for the remaining levers’ effectiveness. The applicability of each type to Ukraine was assessed against documented conditions. A summary matrix “country/instrument → mechanism → applicability” was developed, and sequenced reconstruction-policy implications were formulated. The study integrates the previously separate social-investment, educational, digital, and resilience strands into one framework. An ordered reconstruction toolkit is proposed, prioritizing institutional capacity, the digital advantage, and the educational-fiscal core. The novelty is an applicability matrix of instruments for a post-war recovery country, previously absent from the literature. As the assessments are an analytical extrapolation, future work involves empirical validation on Ukrainian data and a conflict-specific research line. The paper is theoretical.

title: What is sport service quality and how should it be specified?
journal: International Journal of Sports Marketing and Sponsorship
abstract: Purpose Despite its extensive use, the conceptual foundations and operationalization of service quality in sport remain insufficiently clarified. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to delineate the specific evaluative judgments that constitute sport service quality and clarify the construct boundaries separating service quality from related evaluative constructs. Design/methodology/approach A critical review of 85 empirical studies in sport service quality research examined how the construct has been conceptualized, operationalized, and modeled in prior sport management and marketing literature. Studies were coded based on their definitions, measurement approaches, and model specifications. Findings The review reveals that the label “service quality” has been used to refer to three distinct evaluative objects: attribute-level performance perceptions, transaction-specific overall quality judgments, and cumulative global attitudes, without consistently distinguishing among them. Controllable service system elements are also frequently mixed with core sport product evaluations, blurring construct boundaries. Advancing sport service quality theory therefore requires sharper theoretical specification of the judgment object, its temporal scope, and the boundaries of the evaluative construct. Originality/value This study contributes to sport management and marketing literature by proposing a conceptual framework that distinguishes among attribute-level evaluations, transaction-specific overall service quality judgments, and cumulative global attitudes. By grounding service quality within the controllable service delivery system, the proposed framework establishes a clearer basis for the conceptualization and operationalization of service quality in sport.

title: Weakly inhomogeneous solutions to a nonlinear Vlasov–Fokker–Planck equation in a domain
abstract: A nonlinear Vlasov–Fokker–Planck equation is considered in a bounded domain, with specular reflection imposed on the boundary. It is proven that if the initial datum is sufficiently close, in a weighted L ∞ -space, to a radial and spatially homogeneous function that is regular enough, then a corresponding global-in-time weak solution exists, and this one decays with exponential rate to the global Maxwellian. The proof is split into two steps. In the first, the stability of the manifold of spatially homogeneous solutions to this equation is established. In the second part, the close-to-Maxwellian regime is considered. A careful regularization scheme is designed so that this mollified equation can be well-approximated by a linear system. Inspired by the recent preprint [Carrapatoso and Mischler, arxiv:2407.09031], for this linear system, L 2 -hypocoercivity along with ultracontractivity properties are derived in order to change the space of functional decay to the L ∞ -framework. The properties of the original model are then recovered by means of fixed point arguments and carefully passing to the limit of the regularization parameter.

title: The impact of soft power diplomacy on Sino–Japanese rivalry in the Gulf region from 2013 to 2026
journal: Review of Economics and Political Science
abstract: Purpose This research paper analyzes the role of soft power diplomacy as a primary means of advancing the rivalry between China and Japan in consolidating their influence within the Gulf Cooperation Council states, through the cultural dimensions, political values and foreign policies of both sides from 2013 to 2026. Design/methodology/approach This research paper, within its analytical and theoretical framework, relies upon the theoretical framework of the Soft Power Theory, proposed by Joseph Nye. The conceptual framework of the theory was operationalized into key empirical indicators for measurement, specifically the cultural, political values and foreign policy indicators. Additionally, a regional influence indicator was constructed to evaluate the direct outcomes and impacts resulting from these instruments. It also applies the comparative approach to examine the Chinese and Japanese models and determine which is more influential in the Gulf Arab states, based on their similarities and differences. Findings The research finds that China's competitive advantage lies in institutional and developmental soft power through the use of tools such as infrastructure and education. This is particularly achieved by incorporating the Chinese language within national curricula and expanding economic initiatives, especially the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and e-game investments. In contrast, Japan excels in cultural influence by engaging citizens through the “Cool Japan” strategy and the popularity of anime and manga. Additionally, Japan advances knowledge transfer and human capital development under the “Kono Principles,” embedding its identity among Gulf youth. Thus, both models successfully strengthen their influence through these different mechanisms. Originality/value This paper seeks to trace the growing impact of soft power diplomacy on Sino–Japanese rivalry in the Gulf region, an emerging arena, with particular attention to its ability to shape economic partnerships, cultural exchanges and diplomatic influence without military coercion during the period from 2013 to 2026.

title: The Role of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia in Protecting the National Interests of the Russian Federation in the Arctic Region
abstract: One of the most important tasks of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs at the moment is to develop a comprehensive strategic planning document that defines the main areas of activity for the Ministry over the next few years in order to implement the National Security Strategy of the Russian Federation and other related federal strategic planning documents. The author proposes the structural elements of such a comprehensive document related to the activities of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation to protect the national interests of the Russian Federation in the Arctic, including the departmental priority, its goals, objectives (correlated with the objectives of the national priorities of the National Security Strategy and the objectives of the Fundamentals of the State Policy of the Russian Federation in the Arctic for the period up to 2035), the expected results of their solutions and indicators.

title: Teachers’ self-efficacy in supporting learners presenting with autism spectrum disorder in mainstream classrooms
journal: African Journal of Teacher Education and Development
abstract: Background: Teachers’ experiences with supporting learners who are living with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in regular classrooms depend on their self-efficacy beliefs. Albert Bandura’s theory provides constructs of verbal persuasion, emotional state, prior experience, and observation of models, useful for in-service teacher training. Aim: To design, implement, and evaluate an interactive, in-service workshop to equip teachers with knowledge and skills for addressing the high-level needs of learners with ASD. Setting: Mainstream classrooms. Methods: Using qualitative participatory action research, we purposively sampled primary school teachers (n = 20) as participants. We developed the workshop’s content, based on literature and a pre-workshop survey of the teachers’ previous experiences. We facilitated the workshop in collaboration with the participants and conducted a post-workshop survey to evaluate the workshop’s effectiveness. Data were analysed thematically to reveal four themes. Results: Firstly, the challenges teachers’ experience cause doubts in their self-efficacy to support neurodiverse learners. Secondly, teachers relied on informal methods, ad hoc peer support, and minimal use of evidence-based strategies. Thirdly, after participating in the workshop, with hands-on activities, role-playing, and vicarious observations of models, the teachers’ confidence improved as they mastered effective strategies. Lastly, participants valued the effectiveness of the workshop, increasing their self-efficacy. Conclusion: Participatory, collaborative, interactive workshops strengthen teachers’ self-efficacy capacity to address unique ASD learning needs. Contribution: In-service workshops should be designed collaboratively with facilitators actively engaging teachers with accurate knowledge and practical strategies, which enhance self-efficacy to perform specialised didactic practices supporting the increasing prevalence of neurodiverse learners in mainstream classrooms.

title: State-owned enterprises drive sustainable development of agricultural enterprises: supply chain spillover effects based on new quality productivity of enterprises
abstract: Introduction From the perspective of sustainable agricultural development, state-owned enterprises play a crucial role in ensuring the security and development of agricultural industrial and supply chains. They support productivity improvements among agricultural enterprises upstream and downstream in the supply chain, mitigate development risks for agricultural enterprises, and lay the economic foundation for sustainable agricultural development. Against the backdrop of global food system challenges, including supply chain disruptions, climate volatility, and resource constraints, Chinese agricultural enterprises face persistent dilemmas such as weak innovation capacity, high resource dependence, and low marketization. The strategic concept of “new-quality productive forces” has thus emerged as a key framework for driving technology-led and sustainability oriented agricultural transformation. Methods Drawing on the perspective of supply chain spillover effects and utilizing panel data from Chinese A-share listed agricultural companies from 2012 to 2024, this study employs a fixed-effects model, along with bootstrapped mediation analysis and instrumental variable approaches, to examine the impact of state-owned enterprises on the new-quality productive forces of agricultural enterprises upstream and downstream in the supply chain. Results The study finds that state-owned enterprises exert a positive spillover effect on the new-quality productivity of agricultural enterprises upstream and downstream in the supply chain; the higher the proportion of state-owned enterprises in the supply chain, the higher the level of new-quality productivity among agricultural enterprises. Mechanism tests reveal that state-owned enterprises primarily enhance the new-quality productivity of agricultural enterprises by promoting green technological innovation, actively strengthening internal control, and enhancing corporate governance efficiency. The results of the moderating mechanism analysis indicate that media supervision has a positive moderating effect on the supply chain spillover effects of state-owned enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the spillover effects of state-owned enterprises on the new-quality productive forces of agricultural enterprises in the supply chain are more pronounced in the central and western regions. Specifically, the presence of state-owned enterprises on the supplier side has a more significant impact on private enterprises and those with closer regulatory proximity, while the presence of state-owned enterprises on the customer side has a more significant impact on state-owned enterprises themselves and those with more distant regulatory proximity. Discussion In summary, the presence of state-owned enterprises within the supply chain serves as a reserve force for agricultural enterprises, acting as a key driver for enhancing the level of new-quality productivity and achieving high-quality development in the agricultural sector. This finding offers a policy implication: leveraging SOEs as “anchors” in agricultural supply chains can complement direct subsidy policies to foster sustainable agricultural transformation.

title: Developing an open, national-level, small-area geodemographic classification of consumer behaviour
journal: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
abstract: Purpose This study fills a gap in consumer insight by developing an open, national-level small-area geodemographic classification. Existing frameworks overlook localised variations and fail to integrate consumer surveys. Our approach delivers a geodemographic classification of consumer behaviour across England and Wales. Design/methodology/approach We integrated the PDV Consumer Lifestyle Survey, 2021 Census and built-environment accessibility metrics. Spatial microsimulation is used to create synthetic populations at the Lower Super Output Area level, aligning individual attributes with PDV data to produce small-area estimates. Eight analytical domains (i.e. household composition, financial resilience, lifestyle, mobility, online engagement, social networks, shopping patterns and socioeconomic status) were derived from a conceptual frame which is then used to define an iterative variable selection. We then apply clustering to demographic and demand variables to derive primary and subclusters of consumer behaviour. Findings Four clusters emerged, each with distinct demand and demographic profiles. Affluent professional consumers, budget-conscious young urbanites, family-oriented suburban consumers and traditional rural consumers form the main clusters, and then nine further subclusters are derived. Results underscore how the domains derived from the conceptual framework shape small-area patterns. Originality/value Insights can inform targeted policy interventions and retail investment strategies by highlighting the spatial distribution of consumer needs. Opportunities for improving retail centre accessibility, fostering digital inclusion and tailoring product offerings can be derived. This classification lays the groundwork for future methodological advances, such as the use of agent-based modelling to simulate dynamic consumer–retail interactions under varying economic, social and environmental scenarios.
